# Enclii

Compact LLM context index for this repository.

## Read first

- `AGENTS.md` — canonical agent operating instructions.
- `README.md` — human/product overview when present.
- `ECOSYSTEM.md` — MADFAM ecosystem and Enclii deployment context when present.
- `llms-full.txt` — full context map and durable operating contract.

## Platform behaviors agents most often get wrong (updated 2026-09-07)

- One-off jobs (`enclii jobs run-once`): the dispatcher resolves the service's
  Deployment as `<name>`, `<name>-web`, then `<namespace>-web`; deterministic
  admission denials mark the job **failed** with a stored `failure_reason`
  (surfaced by `jobs logs`) instead of pending forever. Full contract:
  `docs/cli/commands/jobs.md`. There is NO `enclii exec` and NO `enclii jobs run <task>`.
- Tunnel routes: switchyard refuses to write or replace an ingress rule whose
  backend Service does not exist with that port, canaries every changed rule and
  reverts dead ones (`ENCLII_TUNNEL_ROUTE_CANARY_ENABLED`, default on), and
  manifest capture refuses to create domain records for a Service doc whose
  name resolves to no live workload. Motivated by the 2026-08-27 identity
  outage: a legacy single-doc manifest's name + declared domains rewrote
  working routes to a dead backend.
- Deploys: `build-publish.yml` (tag v1.0.0-alpha.5+) derives image digests from
  GHCR (`imagetools inspect` on the immutable `:github.sha` tag) — no Actions
  artifacts in the deploy path; the deploy-state-guard fails any run whose pin
  job wrote zero pins.

- DNS records (`providers cloudflare dns-apply`), fixed in #536: for
  **TXT/MX/NS/SRV** a record's identity includes its **content**, so several
  records coexist at one name. Same name+type+content -> `noop`; different
  content -> `create`, leaving the existing records alone; `--replace` (literal
  "true") is the explicit way to overwrite one, and it warns about both the
  value it destroys and the siblings it leaves. CNAME/A/AAAA keep single-record
  update semantics. The dry-run plan is what the apply executes — both decide
  from one live read via one function. Do NOT reach for the Cloudflare
  dashboard to add a second TXT or MX; any runbook step saying so predates
  #536. Before it, a record was keyed by name+type only and a second TXT/MX was
  applied as a destructive `update` of the first (issue #530, hit live on
  2026-09-07: an SPF TXT destroyed a Proton ownership TXT).
- MX priority is a first-class `--priority` flag (#536). The old form — the
  preference inside `--content` as `"10 mail.example.com"` — still works and is
  split back out server-side; the flag wins when both are given, and the
  response reports `priority_source`. A create with no priority defaults to 10
  and says so; a non-numeric or out-of-range value is `invalid_request`, not a
  silent default; priority 0 is legal and preserved. The old `--type MX --apply`
  502 was this: the MX create carried no `priority` field at all, Cloudflare
  answered 400, and every provider error below the handler was rendered 502. A
  record Cloudflare refuses is now 422 (409 duplicate, 424 zone/credential,
  400 bad argument) carrying Cloudflare's own message; 502 is reserved for a
  genuinely unreachable provider, and still does not say whether the write
  landed — re-read the zone before retrying.
- Brand-host onboarding order (verified 2026-09-07): `domains add` **from the
  repo root** (the `-f` parser validates `spec.build.dockerfile` against
  `os.Getwd()`, not the manifest's directory) -> `dns-apply` proxied CNAME ->
  `tunnels-apply` (plan must show only a create for the new host) -> `dns-apply`
  the verification TXT -> `domains verify`. Then `zone-settings-apply` once the
  zone is active (`always_use_https`, `automatic_https_rewrites`,
  `min_tls_version=1.2`; verify `curl -sSI http://<host>/` -> 301). A
  manifest-only merge builds nothing, so no capture runs and a newly declared
  host does not become live. Full runbook:
  `docs/runbooks/DOMAIN_AND_EMAIL_DNS_ONBOARDING.md`.
- After a nameserver switch, clients on a stale resolver see NXDOMAIN for hosts
  that exist only in the new zone (and Cloudflare 1034 for a DNS-only host the
  old zone pointed at a CDN) for up to the old NS TTL. Do not cut over
  redirects, and do not "fix" a record that already reads correctly at the
  zone's own nameservers, until public resolvers agree.
- CLI: `enclii whoami`/`login`/`logout` print on **stderr** (cobra
  `cmd.Println` -> `OutOrStderr()`; the CLI never calls `SetOut`), so
  `whoami > file` captures nothing. `enclii login` resolves whichever Janua
  identity the browser session holds — log out of a client app first.
  **No release carries 2026-09-07's work.** `v1.0.0-alpha.8` was cut 2026-09-06
  from the commit before it, so `--tenant` / `providers porkbun ping` (#527)
  and `dns-apply --priority` plus the non-destructive multi-record fix (#536)
  are all absent. Build from `main` (`go build -o ~/bin/enclii
  ./packages/cli/cmd/enclii`) until `v1.0.0-alpha.9` exists (issue #537). This
  matters beyond missing flags: an alpha.8 `dns-apply` still keys TXT/MX by
  name+type and will destructively overwrite a sibling record that the current
  runbook says is safe to add.
- Per-tenant Porkbun (#527): merging does NOT apply the Vault policy. Run
  `scripts/apply-switchyard-vault-policy-remote.sh` (token on stdin, never
  argv) before the first `--tenant` call, or it 403s and reads as "credentials
  missing". Recipe: `docs/infrastructure/porkbun-tenant-credentials.md`.
- ExternalSecrets under `infra/k8s/base/external-secrets/vault-secrets/` are
  **excluded from ArgoCD**: the `external-secrets-config` Application syncs a
  five-entry `directory.include` allowlist, so a merged change to any of the 19
  per-app manifests is a **silent no-op** — no OutOfSync, no drift alert, no CI
  failure. #535 (a `CTM_RESEND_API_KEY` key on `janua-secrets.yaml`) merged
  green and never reached the cluster; it was applied by a raw JSON patch on the
  live object. Issue #539 tracks the sanctioned path (`enclii secrets es-apply`,
  or reconcile-then-include). Do NOT assume merging a `vault-secrets/*.yaml`
  change deploys it. Doc: `docs/infrastructure/EXTERNAL_SECRETS.md`.
- ExternalSecret ordering: **Vault property first, manifest second.** An
  ExternalSecret is all-or-nothing — one missing property fails the whole sync
  and the target Secret keeps its old data, or on a first sync is never created.
  Use `vault kv patch` when the path exists and `vault kv put` when it does not:
  KV v2 answers **404** to a patch on a never-written path. #529 retired the
  committed Verdaccio Secret in the same change that introduced its
  ExternalSecret replacement, so ArgoCD pruned the old value before the Vault
  key existed (fixed in #534).
- Reloader reads `reloader.stakater.com/auto` on the **Deployment's own
  `metadata.annotations`**, never on the pod template. An annotation on the
  template is silently inert — Verdaccio carried one there since 2026-05 and it
  never fired, so a rotated htpasswd left the pod serving the kubelet's stale
  projection while reporting `Ready` (#534).
- npm.madfam.io credentials do not mix: a **Janua API key** (`jnk_…`) goes in
  `_auth` (HTTP Basic) and NEVER in `_authToken` — `security.api.jwt` makes
  Verdaccio verify a Bearer token as its own JWT before any plugin runs, and the
  failure degrades to *anonymous* rather than 401, so the key is never seen. An
  **htpasswd password** (e.g. the rotated admin) uses
  `npm login --auth-type=legacy` (without it npm tries a web login flow this
  registry does not serve). The **CI service token** is a Verdaccio-issued JWT
  and does belong in `_authToken`. htpasswd itself is Vault-sourced
  (`secret/npm-registry #htpasswd` -> ExternalSecret `verdaccio-auth`), never
  committed; rotate one-shot with
  `scripts/operator/npm-registry-admin-password-rotate.sh`. Doc:
  `docs/infrastructure/npm-registry.md`.
- Cloudflare **Redirect Rules** have no Enclii op (issue #538). The 2026-09-07
  brand-migration 301s (`crea-map.madfam.io` -> `map.creatumundo.mx`,
  `crea-erp` -> `erp`) were created in the dashboard as documented break-glass.
  The source host must keep a **proxied** DNS record or the rule never fires.
  Break-glass procedure: `docs/runbooks/DOMAIN_AND_EMAIL_DNS_ONBOARDING.md`.

## Production operations

Routine production operations are Enclii-first. Use Enclii web, API, or CLI
before raw infrastructure tools. Direct `kubectl`, `helm`, SSH, provider CLIs,
`docker exec`, or direct container access is bootstrap/break-glass only.
